summary_en: Aomori, at Japan's northern tip of Honshu, is covered on the site by a series of column articles: '8 Things to Do in Aomori' (castle, onsen, Lake Towada/Oirase, Hakkoda, Nebuta, rice-paddy art), '5 Must-Visit Sightseeing Spots' (Hakkoda, Towada, Oirase, Osorezan, Hotokegaura), a 2025 travel guide, autumn foliage, the Nebuta Festival, UNESCO Jomon sites, Furukawa Fish Market, Takayama Inari Shrine, A-Factory and a local food guide.

summary_en: Hirosaki, a castle town in western Aomori, is covered by articles on Hirosaki Castle (1611, Tsugaru clan, one of the 100 Fine Castles of Japan, cherry blossom festival 23 April–5 May, botanical garden, winter Snow Lantern Festival), a summer guide (Shirakami-Sanchi and the Hirosaki Neputa Festival, 1–7 August) and Hirosaki Apple Park with apple picking and the Kimori Cider Factory.

attractions.description_en: Built in 1611 by the Tsugaru clan; one of the '100 Fine Castles of Japan', with over 2,600 cherry trees and the Hirosaki Cherry Blossom Festival (23 April–5 May).
The historic castle keep houses exhibits on the Tsugaru domain's feudal history.
Garden within the castle grounds with more than 1,200 plant species in thematic zones.
Winter festival with hundreds of glowing snow lanterns, ice sculptures and projection mapping on the castle grounds.
Held every year 1–7 August; designated an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan.
UNESCO World Natural Heritage beech forest about 30 minutes by car from central Hirosaki, with clear streams and mountain scenery.
Apple orchards where guests can pick apples from early August to mid-November.
Cidery in the apple park area offering tastings of alcoholic and non-alcoholic ciders from locally grown fruit.

summary_en: Nagano is the site's most densely covered prefecture: a Nagano City travel guide, '5 Must-Do Activities', Zenko-ji & Togakushi, the Snow Monkey Park, family activities, top 5 onsen, shopping, Anrakuji Temple, Nagano Olympics sites, Matsushiro samurai district, Kamikochi and Hakuba guides, plus the Ina Valley (treated separately).

attractions.description_en: Founded in the 7th century with over 1,400 years of history and said to hold Japan's first Buddhist statue; features the Okaidan Meguri pitch-dark passage where visitors search for the 'Key to Paradise'.

attractions.description_en: Mountain shrine complex north of Nagano City, paired with Zenko-ji in a dedicated article.

attractions.description_en: Alpine valley in the Northern Japan Alps with clear rivers, forests and scenic hiking trails; dedicated travel guide.

summary_en: Fukuoka coverage centres on a '2 Days in Fukuoka' itinerary article (Shikanoshima Island, Shikaumi Shrine, Hakata Old Town, Kushida Shrine, yatai stalls) plus dedicated pieces on Tochoji Temple's 10 m wooden Buddha, Ohori Park, the Fukuoka Castle Ruins and the Couple Stones of Sakurai Futamigaura in Itoshima. The site also sells a 6-day 'Discover Fukuoka' sample itinerary.

summary_en: A single day-trip article covers Kamakura, the political centre of Japan in the Kamakura period (1185–1333), highlighting Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, the Great Buddha of Kotoku-in, Hasedera, Engakuji, Hokokuji's bamboo grove and Komachi-dori shopping street.

attractions.description_en: Shrine dedicated to Hachiman, closely linked to the Minamoto clan and the samurai era.
Bronze Great Buddha 13.35 m tall and about 121 tonnes, Japan's second tallest bronze Buddha.
Called the 'Temple of Flowers' for its hillside plantings that change with the seasons.
One of the main Zen temples of Kamakura.
Known for its famous bamboo grove.
Popular shopping street near Kamakura Station for local food and souvenirs.

summary_en: The Shimokita Peninsula at the northernmost tip of Honshu is covered through Oma tuna articles (Oma bluefin 'black diamonds', a June–October tuna-fishing experience), the Aomori 2025 guide (Osorezan, Yagen Valley, coastal towns) and the 5-spots article (Osorezan, Hotokegaura). The site's 5-day Premium Tohoku Gourmet Tour is built around Oma tuna and Shimokita.

attractions.description_en: Town at the northernmost tip of Honshu famed for bluefin tuna ('black diamonds') fattened by the meeting currents of the Tsugaru Strait; fishing boats come and go in the harbour.

attractions.description_en: About 50-minute boat ride through Tenryukyo Gorge, a nationally designated scenic spot.

attractions.name_ja: 駒ヶ岳ロープウェイ・千畳敷カール

summary_en: The Matsumoto Castle Travel Guide covers the castle keep, gardens and seasonal festivals (cherry blossom in April, Taiko Drum Festival in July, Ice Carving Festival in January), plus Nakamachi Street's kura storehouses, the Matsumoto City Museum of Art (Yayoi Kusama) and Fukashi Shrine.

attractions.description_en: Preserved wooden interiors, historic weapon displays and panoramic views from the top floor; castle reflected in the moat, best in spring and autumn.
Spring Cherry Blossom Festival (April), Taiko Drum Festival (July) and Ice Carving Festival (January) held at the castle.
Historic shopping street of kura-zukuri storehouses with shops, cafes, sake breweries and handicrafts.
Celebrates Matsumoto-born artist Yayoi Kusama's polka-dot works alongside contemporary exhibits.
Tranquil shrine a short walk from the castle.

attractions.description_en: UNESCO World Heritage temple famous for its Pure Land garden, largely unchanged for centuries.

attractions.description_en: Main hall, artifact repository and the Kaizando hall honouring Tendai leaders and the Fujiwara lords of Hiraizumi.

The 5-day 'Discover Osaka' itinerary adds a tea ceremony at the Sakai Plaza of Rikyu and Akiko, kofun burial mounds and teamLab at Nagai Botanical Garden.

131 m tower across from Kyoto Station with panoramic views over temples to the surrounding mountains.
Roughly 2 km canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees, about 30 minutes at a leisurely pace.
Hanami park known for its large weeping cherry tree and food stalls at peak bloom.

attractions.description_en: One of the most historically significant shrines in the Chita area, dedicated to Omononushi (safety, prosperity, protection).
Oldest lighthouse in Aichi (first lit 1921), 18 m tall, white silhouette over Mikawa Bay in Mihama.
Built in the early 17th century by Tokugawa Ieyasu as a key Edo-period defensive base.

Open-air museum in Inuyama preserving more than 60 relocated, restored Meiji-era (1868–1912) buildings.

summary_en: '6 Hidden Gems in Suwa' covers the Lake Suwa area: Suwa Taisha, Tateishi Park ('Your Name' viewpoint), the 1928 Katakurakan bathhouse, the five Suwa Gokura sake breweries, Takashima Castle and Yokoya Gorge.

attractions.description_en: One of Japan's oldest and most esteemed Shinto shrines, head shrine of over 10,000 Suwa shrines nationwide.
Hillside park with panoramic views over Lake Suwa; said to be a model for a backdrop in the film 'Your Name'.
Historic public bathhouse built in 1928, originally a guesthouse for silk magnates and dignitaries.
Five historic breweries clustered in Kamisuwa: Masumi, Reijin, Honkin, Maihime and Yokobue.
'Floating Castle of Suwa', reconstructed in 1970; keep houses a small museum of local samurai history.
Waterfalls, mossy rocks and a mostly flat, family-friendly 6 km trail along the Shibu River.

summary_en: 'Things to Do in Oita' presents Japan's 'Onsen Prefecture' (5,093 natural hot springs): Yufuin's Yunotsubo Kaido street and foot baths, Yufuin Floral Village, Beppu's steaming streets and the seven Hells (Jigoku Meguri), plus local dishes toriten and jigoku-mushi.

Lake at the end of Yunotsubo Kaido with foot baths nearby.

attractions.description_en: Cotswolds-inspired village of flower-lined paths, shops, cafes and an owl experience.
Seven geothermal 'hells' near 100°C, including cobalt-blue Umi Jigoku and red Chinoike Jigoku; Beppu has Japan's highest number of hot springs.
Oita comfort food served with kabosu citrus, mustard and ponzu or soy sauce.
Ingredients cooked with natural hot-spring steam.

attractions.description_en: One of Japan's best-preserved post towns, among the first protected by national preservation law; hidden cables, car-free centre, wooden ryokan, teahouses and restored honjin.
Hillside post town with a steep stone-paved slope, inns, teahouses, craft shops, water wheels and Kiso Valley views.
Roughly 7–8 km section of the Nakasendo, about 2.5–3 hours at a relaxed pace.
